# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 12 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_012_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 4

**1** After fifteen days, during which I had fasted and earnestly sought the Lord, the meaning of the writing was revealed to me. The writing read as follows: **2** "Your offspring have sinned against God, Hermas, and they have blasphemed the Lord and betrayed their parents through great wickedness. They were rightly called betrayers of their parents, yet even in betraying them they gained nothing — they only added more transgressions to their existing sins. **3** Riotous living and all manner of wanton wickedness were added on top, so that the full measure of your children's transgressions has been reached. **4** Yet you know that God is merciful and will restore the sins of your household, if you repent with your whole household and humble yourselves before the Lord and serve him with pure hearts — then he will heal all your former sins." **5** "Do not lose heart over your household's condition, but continue to admonish them. For just as a goldsmith refines his work by fire, so God refines those who belong to him — especially those who are his own." There the message ended.

---

*LOGOS note: "full measure of transgressions" echoes the Daniel/Maccabean concept of sin reaching its fullness (cf. Dan 8:23; 2 Macc 6:14). The goldsmith simile parallels the blacksmith simile in ch. 2.*
